settings.name_in_paper: contextual MAB problem with stochastic payoffs (similarity space)
unmapped: Expected payoff mu(x,y) is 1-Lipschitz w.r.t. a known similarity metric D on context-arm pairs (compact similarity space, diameter <= 1)
Set of feasible context-arm pairs P may be a strict subset of X x Y
Oracle access to the similarity space
settings.definition_quote: In each round $t$ ... a context $x_t\in X$ is revealed to the algorithm, the algorithm chooses an arm $y_t\in Y$ such that $(x_t,y_t) \in \mP$, payoff (reward) $\pi_t\in [0,1]$ is revealed. The sequence of context arrivals is fixed before the first round ... $R(T) \triangleq \sum_{t=1}^T \mu(x_t, y_t) - \mu^*(x_t)$

settings.name_in_paper: contextual MAB with stochastic payoffs, product similarity space (lower bound)
unmapped: Product similarity space D = min(1, D_X + D_Y), arbitrary given
Lower bound is in expectation over a distribution of instances
settings.definition_quote: Consider the contextual MAB problem with stochastic payoffs, Let $(\mP,\D)$ be a product similarity space.

unmapped: Expected payoff of each arm changes by at most a known volatility sigma per round (|mu(t,y)-mu(t',y)| <= sigma|t-t'|)
Volatility sigma known a priori to the algorithm
settings.definition_quote: we assume that expected payoff of each arm $y$ changes by at most $\sigma_y$ in each round, for some a-priori known volatilities $\sigma_y$ ... We call this setting the drifting MAB problem.

unmapped: Similarity D((t,y),(t',y')) = min(1, sigma|t-t'| + D_Y(y,y')) with known volatility sigma
Arms space has covering dimension d with multiplier k
Expected payoffs evolve by mutually independent stochastic processes with uniform [0,1] marginals at each time, satisfying |mu(t,y)-mu(t',y)| <= sigma|t-t'| with known sigma
Regret is averaged over the processes Gamma
settings.definition_quote: we assume that expected payoffs $\mu(\cdot,y)$ of each arm $y$ evolve over time according to some stochastic process $\Gamma_y$ that satisfies~(temporal constraint). We assume that the processes $\Gamma_y$ are mutually independent, and moreover that the marginal distributions $\mu(t,y)$ are uniform on $[0,1]$

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic MAB (random walk with reflecting boundaries)
unmapped: Expected payoff of each arm is an independent random walk with step +-sigma on [0,1] with reflecting boundaries, 1/sigma integer; sigma known
Dynamic regret against best arm each round, averaged over the random walks
settings.definition_quote: Here for each arm $y$ the stochastic process $\Gamma_y$ is a random walk with step $\pm \sigma_y$. To ensure that the random walk stays within the interval $[0,1]$, we assume reflecting boundaries.

settings.name_in_paper: sleeping MAB problem with stochastic payoffs
unmapped: Sequence of awake sets fixed in advance; regret against best awake arm each round
settings.definition_quote: We model sleeping bandits as contextual MAB problem where each context arrival $x_t$ corresponds to the set of arms that are ``awake" in this round.

settings.name_in_paper: contextual MAB problem with adversarial payoffs
unmapped: Payoff functions drawn from time-specific distributions Pi_t fixed in advance (randomized oblivious adversary)
mu_t Lipschitz on product space (X x Y, D_X + D_Y) and mu*_t Lipschitz on context space
Benchmark: best context-specific arm y*(x) maximizing sum_t mu_t(x,y)
Black-box bandit subroutine with known convergence time T_0(r) = c_Y r^{-(2+d_Y)} log(1/r)
settings.definition_quote: For each round $t$, there is a payoff function $\hat{\pi}_t: X\times Y \to [0,1]$ ... sampled independently from a time-specific distribution $\Pi_t$ ... Distributions $\Pi_t$ are fixed by the adversary in advance ... $R(T) \triangleq \sum_{t=1}^T \mu_t(x_t, y_t) - \mu^*_t(x_t)$

symbols.c_cov: multiplier c in the covering-type dimension (any c>0)
symbols.d_c: contextual zooming dimension with multiplier c

source.label: thm:ZoomAlg
source.quote: Consider the contextual MAB problem with stochastic payoffs. There is an algorithm (namely, Algorithm~\ref{alg:contextual-zooming} described below) whose contextual regret $R(T)$ satisfies~\refeq{eq:regret-covNum} with $N_r$ equal to $N_r(\mPzoom)$, the $r$-zooming number. Consequently, $R(T)$ satisfies the dimension-type guarantee~\refeq{eq:regret-dim}, where $d_c$ is the contextual zooming dimension.

results.notes: Also gives N_r-type bound R(T) <= C_0 inf_{r0} (r0 T + sum_{r=2^-i >= r0} N_r log T / r) with N_r the r-zooming number. Paper does not specify expectation vs random regret explicitly; regret defined via means. Worst case (covering dimension of similarity space) recovers T^{1-1/(2+d_X+d_Y)} log T.

bound.expression_latex: R(T) \leq O(C_0)\,(c\,T^{1-1/(2+d_c)}\, \log T), C_0 = doubling constant times absolute constant

symbols.c_dbl: doubling constant of the similarity space
symbols.d_c: covering-type dimension induced by the adjusted r-zooming number

source.label: thm:ZoomAlg-adjusted
source.quote: Consider the contextual MAB problem with stochastic payoffs. The contextual regret $R(T)$ of the contextual zooming algorithm satisfies~\refeq{eq:regret-covNum}, where $N_r$ is the adjusted $r$-zooming number and $C_0$ is the doubling constant of the similarity space times some absolute constant. Consequently, $R(T)$ satisfies the dimension-type guarantee~\refeq{eq:regret-dim}, where $d_c$ is the corresponding covering-type dimension.

results.notes: No proof given (sketch omitted). Dimension-type form recorded.

symbols.R_target: arbitrary positive number R <= R_UB(T), the pessimistic upper bound (eq. regret-covNum with N_r = packing number of P); instances in the hard distribution have zooming upper bound O(R)

conditions: instance drawn from a constructed distribution I over instances with 0-1 payoffs, each satisfying R_UB_mu(T) <= O(R)

source.label: thm:LBs-strong
source.quote: Consider the contextual MAB problem with stochastic payoffs, Let $(\mP,\D)$ be a product similarity space. Fix an arbitrary time horizon $T$ and a positive number $R\leq \regretUB(T)$. Then there exists a distribution $\mI$ over problem instances on $(\mP,\D)$ with the following two properties: (a) $\regretUB_{\mu}(T) \leq O(R)$ for each problem instance in support(I). (b) for any contextual bandit algorithm it holds that $\E_{\mI}[R(T)] \geq \Omega(R/\log T)$

results.notes: Matches Theorem 4.1 up to log factors for any value of the upper bound. Expectation over random instance from I.

bound.regime: T = N_inst*r_scale**(-2), r_scale in (0,1/2], N_inst <= N_r(P)

symbols.N_inst: parameter N <= N_r(P), r-packing number of the similarity space

conditions: instance chosen uniformly at random from the needle-in-haystack family I_{N,r} with 0-1 payoffs

source.label: lm:LB
source.quote: Fix $r\in (0,\tfrac12]$ and $N\leq N_r(\mP)$. Let $\mI = \mI_{N,r}$ and $T_0 = N\,r^{-2}$. Then: (i) for each problem instance in $\mI$ it holds that $\regretUB_{\mu}(T_0) \leq O(N/r)(\log T_0)$. (ii) any contextual bandit algorithm has regret $\E_{\mI}[R(T_0)] \geq \Omega(N/r)$ for a problem instance chosen uniformly at random from $\mI$.

results.notes: Part (ii) recorded; part (i) bounds the upper-bound expression on these instances.

symbols.sigma_v: volatility: max per-round change of each arm's expected payoff

conditions: all volatilities equal sigma (paper remarks same bound with average volatility)

source.label: cor:driftingMAB-pessimistic
source.quote: Consider the drifting MAB problem with $k$ arms and volatilities $\sigma_y\equiv \sigma$. Contextual zooming with period $T_0$ has average dynamic regret $\hat{R}(T) = O(k\sigma \log T_0)^{1/3}$, whenever $T\geq T_0\geq (\tfrac{k}{\sigma^2})^{1/3}\, \log \tfrac{k}{\sigma}$.

results.notes: Paper bounds average dynamic regret R(T)/T; multiplied by T. Paper claims optimal up to log factors (details omitted).

symbols.d_Y: covering dimension of the arms space
symbols.c_cov: multiplier k of the covering dimension of the arms space

source.label: cor:driftingMAB-spatial
source.quote: Consider the drifting MAB problem with spatial constraints~\refeq{eq:driftingMAB-spatial}, where $\sigma$ is the volatility. Let $d$ be the covering dimension of the arms space, with multiplier $k$. Contextual zooming with period $T_0$ has average dynamic regret $\hat{R}(T) = O(k\, \sigma \log T_0)^{\tfrac{1}{d+3}}$, whenever $T\geq T_0 \geq k^{\tfrac{1}{d+3}} \; \sigma^{-\tfrac{d+2}{d+3}} \; \log \tfrac{k}{\sigma}$.

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by T. Here k is the covering multiplier, not number of arms.

source.label: cor:driftingMAB-marginals
source.quote: Consider drifting MAB with uniform marginals, with $k$ arms and volatilities $\sigma_y\equiv \sigma$. Contextual zooming with period $T_0$ satisfies $\E_\Gamma[\hat{R}(T)] = O(k\,\sigma^{2/3}\,\log T_0)$, whenever $T\geq T_0\geq \sigma^{-2/3} \log\tfrac{1}{\sigma}$.

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by T; expectation over payoff processes Gamma.

tuning: contextual zooming parameterized by similarity space D_{T_0} = min(1, sigma|t-t'|^{1/2} log T_0 + 1{y != y'})

source.label: cor:DynamicMAB
source.quote: Consider the Dynamic MAB problem with $k$ arms and volatilities $\sigma_y\equiv \sigma$. Let $\mathtt{ALG}_{T_0}$ denote the contextual zooming algorotihm with period $T_0$ which is parameterized by the similarity space $(\mP,\D_{T_0})$. Then $\mathtt{ALG}_{T_0}$ satisfies $\E_\Gamma[\hat{R}(T)] = O(k\,\sigma\,\log^2 T_0)$, whenever $T\geq T_0\geq \tfrac{1}{\sigma} \log\tfrac{1}{\sigma}$.

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by T; matches Slivkins & Upfal 2008.

bound.regime: for every r_0 > 0 (bound is the infimum over r_0)

symbols.G_r0: sum over arms i with Delta_adj_i > r_0 of 1/Delta_adj_i
symbols.Delta_adj_i: mu_{i+1} - mu_i after sorting arms by increasing mean

source.quote: Consider the sleeping MAB problem with stochastic payoffs. Order the arms so that their expected payoffs are $\mu_1\leq \mu_2 \leq \ldots \leq \mu_n$, where $n$ is the number of arms. Let $\Delta_i = \mu_{i+1}-\mu_i$. Then $R(T) \leq \inf_{r>0} ( rT + \sum_{i:\, \Delta_i>r}\; \frac{O(\log T)}{\Delta_i} )$.

results.notes: Delta_i here are gaps between consecutive sorted means, not canonical gaps. Recovers Kleinberg et al. 2008 sleeping bandits result.

symbols.c_X: multiplier for relaxed covering dimension of context arrivals (any c_X>0)
symbols.d_X: relaxed covering dimension of context arrivals with multiplier c_X and slack T_0(.)
symbols.c_Y: constant in convergence time of the subroutine Bandit
symbols.d_Y: exponent in convergence time T_0(r) = c_Y r^{-(2+d_Y)} log(1/r)

conditions: for the fixed-context case, convergence time of Bandit is at most c_Y r^{-(2+d_Y)} log(1/r) on the problem class
tuning: c_Y and d_Y known to the algorithm
